subject: Food Science
title: Biological Hazards
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Biological Hazards.

hook.text: Each year, 600 million people get sick from contaminated food. Biological hazards—bacteria, viruses, parasites—are the top cause.

buildup.text: Biological hazards include pathogenic bacteria, viruses, parasites, and prions. Each enters food through different routes.

discovery.text: Bacteria cause the most foodborne illness cases. Norovirus causes the most outbreaks. Parasites are hardest to detect.

twist.text: Not all biological hazards respond to cooking. Norovirus on salad and toxins pre-formed by Staph survive heat.

climax.text: The WHO estimates foodborne disease kills 420,000 people annually. Children under 5 bear 40% of that burden.

punchline.text: Bacteria, viruses, parasites—invisible killers in food. Prevention is the only defense.

quiz.question: Which biological hazard causes the most foodborne outbreaks?
